patient_summary: 52-year-old adult ED patient with pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea, low Wells category (synthetic).
pretest_source: Wells 2001 Results, p. 102 (also Abstract p. 98, Figure 2 p. 103): low-probability group, 7 of 527 (1.3%, CI 0.5-2.7%) had PE.
result_shown: ELISA D-dimer below the assay cutoff (500 ng/mL FEU)

sources.location: p. 102, Results text (Abstract p. 98; group sizes in Figure 2, p. 103)

sources.quantity: LR+ 1.68 (1.44-1.95), LR- 0.13 (0.03-0.58), ELISA, PE studies, Tier 1 analysis

conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.
notes: Positive-result variant is weakly informative. Assay mismatch: the prior is from a cohort that used the SimpliRED whole-blood agglutination assay (Wells 2001 p. 97 and throughout), while the LRs are for the ELISA class (Stein 2004 Tier 1). For the whole-blood assay class Stein 2004 Table 1 (p. 593) gives PE LR+ 2.93 (1.89-4.52), LR- 0.31 (0.18-0.51); Tier 2 ELISA PE is LR+ 1.97, LR- 0.08 (0.01-0.43). The Wells cohort's own implied LR- is about 0.34 to 0.51: 2 of the 7 low-probability PE had a negative D-dimer (diagnosed by high-probability V/Q scan at presentation, p. 102 and Figure 2 footnote, p. 103) and 1 more of the 437 D-dimer-negative low-probability patients had PE in follow-up (Abstract p. 98; low-group NPV printed as 99.5%, p. 102), so 2 to 3 of 7 PE were D-dimer negative (approximate; LR- = (k/7)/((437-k)/520) for k = 2, 3). Primary band = Bayes over the Stein Tier 1 ELISA LR CIs at the Wells prior. Wells score as written in the note (items from data/notes/facts/B1_pe_low.json): DVT signs 0; PE leading consideration 0 (viral pleurisy judged more likely); HR 88, 0; immobilization or surgery 0; prior PE or DVT 0; hemoptysis 0; malignancy 0. Total 0 = low (<2). Age 52 is not a Wells item; it keeps the patient PERC-positive (age >= 50) so a D-dimer is a guideline-plausible order (L3).
